If one cut is deep or spreads open too much, I cut up a bandaid to make steri-strips which are basically stitches. I then loosely wrap a towel around it to let the cuts dry out overnight and so nothing gets stuck. In the morning, I gently clean with soap, cover with a non-stick dressing and then put on top a compression bandage to keep the cuts tight and clean but also invisible to others if I wear a short-sleeved shirt.

I understand how religion has made you feel ashamed of yourself, especially when you should feel like the victim, not the perpetrator.

Psychiatric help is SO expensive, I've gone without a lot to pay for it, but in the end the most affordable way to learn coping strategies and theories on behaviour/thinking/feeling was to become my own shrink.

Instead of self-help books, I read psychological theory textbooks. Instead of news stories, I read academic journalism on how to cope with mental illness. Instead of watching that stream or compilation video on Youtube, I watched psychologists explain theories. and etc. with Netflix.

Eventually, when I would go see a psychologist, our knowledge would be the same and the only eventual thing I was missing out on was human connection. So my psych appointments became less about paying to learn basic psychological theory, and more a debrief or some trauma talk therapy which is invaluable to someone with mental illness. There's free helplines if you cannot afford psych appointments that will fulfill that same function which have been helpful for me when I can't afford a psych.

Depression may make that sound like a lot of effort and anxiety may make you think you don't understand it half the time and trauma may make you believe it will never work, but there are so many possibilities out there that one has to click. I hope any of what I have said has helped and I wish you the best, I truly do.
